verses.1: My son, give attention to my wisdom; incline your ear to my understanding.
verses.2: That you may keep discretion and instruction, and that my words may guard you.
verses.3: For a harlot offers her lips like honey, and her mouth is smoother than oil.
verses.4: But in the end she is bitter as gall, sharp as a two-edged sword.
verses.5: Her feet descend to death, her steps lead to Sheol, and her paths are not known.
verses.6: She leads away the path of life, her tracks are unsteady and not recognizable.
verses.7: Now then, my sons, listen to me, and do not turn away from my words.
verses.8: Keep your distance from her, do not draw near to the entrance of her house.
verses.9: Lest you give your honor to another, your years to the cruel.
verses.10: Lest strangers be satisfied with your strength, and your toils be in the house of another.
verses.11: You will be in anguish in the end, when your flesh and bones are worn out.
verses.12: And you will say, "How I hated discipline! My heart resented correction!
verses.13: I did not listen to the voice of my teacher, nor did I incline my ear to my instructor."
verses.14: I was nearly ruined by all evil, in the midst of a crowd and a gathering.
verses.15: Drink water from your own cistern, and flowing waters from your own well.
verses.16: Let your fountains overflow in the streets, let your streams flow in the public squares.
verses.17: Let them belong to you alone, and no stranger share in them.
verses.18: Let your fountain be blessed, and rejoice with the wife of your youth.
verses.19: A loving hind, a graceful doe— may her breasts satisfy you at all times, may you be intoxicated always in her love.
verses.20: And why, my son, should you be drawn to a strange woman, embrace the bosom of another?
verses.21: For the ways of a man are before the eyes of the LORD, and He searches out all his steps.
verses.22: The iniquities of the wicked will catch him, and he will be ensnared in the cords of his own sins.
verses.23: He will die without instruction, and in the abundance of his folly he will be lost.

notes:
Notes
- v. 3: "her lips like honey" is a common metaphor in Hebrew, and "honey" is used as a direct translation of דְּבַשׁ.
- v. 19: "a loving hind, a graceful doe" renders אַיֶּלֶת אֲהָבִים and יַעֲלַת־חֵן, respectively. "hind" and "doe" are traditional renderings of these terms in English Bibles.
- v. 21: "before the eyes of the LORD" is a direct translation of נֹכַח עֵינֵי יְהוָה, preserving the active sense of divine observation.
